name: Contribution per Unit
description: Calculate the contribution margin earned on each unit sold.
formula: Contribution per unit = Price per unit − Variable cost per unit
business_contexts: a manufacturer pricing a unit sold to distributors
a food truck pricing a menu item against ingredient cost
a hardware brand pricing a device against its bill of materials
a print shop pricing a job against material cost
a bottler pricing a case against production cost
question_patterns: Given the price and variable cost per unit below, what is the contribution margin per unit?
Calculate the per-unit contribution margin from the figures given.
What is the profit contributed by each unit sold, given the price and cost below?
Calculate the margin earned on each unit from the values shown.
Using the price and variable cost given, what does each unit contribute?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate contribution per unit = price_per_unit − variable_cost_per_unit
key_insight: Contribution per unit is the foundation under breakeven, capacity, and pricing math — every one of those formulas starts by subtracting variable cost from price.
common_mistakes: Subtracting fixed costs, which don't belong at the per-unit level
Reversing the subtraction and reporting a negative contribution
framework_soundbite: Contribution is what's left after the unit pays for itself — price minus variable cost, nothing else.
